name: word-pattern-substitution
plaintext: Geologists followed the creek upstream until the gravel turned from gray river stone to a band of red shale. They measured the dip of each layer and wrote the numbers in a field book before the rain could smear them. One outcrop showed ripples that had hardened when the water was shallow and warm. Another held broken shells the size of a thumbnail. The party ate lunch on a flat boulder and argued, without any heat, about whether the ridge had been a beach or a delta. By late afternoon they had samples enough to justify the long walk back to the wagon. A quick extra box of quartz fixed the last gap in the section.

keys.key_direction: ciphertext A-Z to plaintext; expected output only, never a search input

note: Constructed repository monoalphabetic substitution fixture, not a published historical decipherment. Ciphertext is a literal independent vector from SUBSTITUTION_PLAIN and the repository substitution permutation. The solver receives only ciphertext, the listed lexicon, and bounds; expected_decrypt_key is checked only after recovery. The AIMA source is an algorithm reference for CSP backtracking with minimum remaining values and forward checking, not a source for the fixture plaintext. Every word must belong to the supplied lexicon. A unique plaintext is unique only within that lexicon and substitution model, and does not imply a uniquely determined key when ciphertext letters are absent. No solve of Kryptos K4, Zodiac, Beale, McCormick, Voynich, army message Nr. 86, or an unknown script is claimed.
